extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, appointed agents/representatives and patent practitioners filing or prosecuting PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements for handling international (PCT) applications during the international phase, including rectification of obvious mistakes, amendments, withdrawals, time limits, filing modalities, and confidentiality/publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to request rectification of an obvious mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office, the International Searching Authority, the International Preliminary Authority or the International Bureau discovers what appears to be a rectifiable obvious mistake in the international application or in any other document, it may invite the applicant to file a request for rectification under Rule 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent authorities may proactively invite the applicant to request rectification of an obvious mistake (Rule 91.1(h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and notification on rectification requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the applicant has filed a request for rectification of an obvious mistake, the competent authority promptly decides whether to authorize or to refuse the requested rectification and promptly notifies its decision to the applicant and the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of a refusal, the competent authority should inform the applicant and the International Bureau of the reasons for the refusal. Where authorized, the document shall be rectified in accordance with the Administrative Instructions (Sections 325, 413bis, 511 and 607). If authorization is received before completion of technical preparations for publication, the IB publishes rectified sheets as part of the international application; if after, the IB will republish in accordance with Rule 48.2(i). If authorized by the IPEA, rectified sheets and the request are annexed to the IPRP (Chapter II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rectification of an obvious mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: If the mistake appears in the international application as filed, the rectification becomes effective as from the international filing date; if the mistake appears in any document other than the international application as filed, the rectification becomes effective as from the date on which that document was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 91.3(c) — effective date depends on which document contained the mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when rectification authorization is refused
rubrics_metrics.description: If the authorization of a rectification is refused, the applicant may request the International Bureau, within two months from the date of the refusal, in writing, to publish the request for rectification, the reasons for refusal by the authority and any further brief comments that may be submitted by the applicant, together with the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This request requires payment of a special fee (Annex B (IB)). Once published, the applicant may pursue rectification before designated Offices under national law. Refused requests are not annexed to the IPRP except in certain circumstances (see paragraph 10.076).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of authorized rectification on designated/elected Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated and elected Offices must process the international application 'as rectified', unless that Office has already started processing or examination before notification of authorization under Rule 91.3(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A designated/elected Office may disregard a rectification authorized under Rule 91.1 only if it finds it would not have authorized the rectification if it had been the competent authority; but it may disregard only after giving applicant an opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities to amend claims, description and drawings during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: During the international phase the applicant has one opportunity to amend the claims under Article 19 after receiving the international search report; amendments may also be made under Article 34(2)(b) to the description, claims and drawings before and during the international preliminary examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments are in addition to corrections under Article 11/Rule 20 and Article 14/Rule 26, and to rectification of obvious mistakes under Rule 91. Applicants also have opportunities to amend for purposes of the national phase by Articles 28 and 41 (see National Chapters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language for submission of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: There are specific language requirements for amendments: amendments of claims under Article 19 and amendments under Article 34 must be submitted in specified languages (refer to paragraphs 9.004, 9.017-9.019, and 10.071).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 46.3 and Rule 55.3 and the referenced paragraphs for detail; translations may be required depending on whether a translation of the international application was transmitted for ISR, supplementary search, publication or IPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: No addition of new matter in amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 19(2) and Article 34(2)(b) provide that amendments are not to go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is not checked during the international phase unless the applicant requests international preliminary examination. If the IPEA considers amendments go beyond original disclosure it will comment in written opinion and in the IPRP and the report will be established as if such amendment had not been made. National Offices may check during national phase and adverse consequences (disallowance or later filing date) may result. National law may differ; the PCT does not bind Contracting States to this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheets must be accompanied by a letter indicating basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sheets submitted with Article 19 or Article 34 amendments must be accompanied by a letter indicating the basis for the amendment in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive compliance is not checked during the international phase unless IPE requested. If IPEA finds replacement sheets lack such a letter or it fails to indicate the basis, the IPEA may establish the IPRP as if the amendment had not been made. National Offices may also check and failure may result in disallowance of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the international application by a notice addressed to the International Bureau or the receiving Office (or to the IPEA where Article 39(1) applies), received before the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Any such withdrawal is free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of withdrawal must be signed by all applicants. An appointed agent or common representative may sign on behalf of those who appointed them, but a 'deemed common representative' may not sign on behalf of other applicants. Waiver of separate power of attorney does not apply to notices of withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal on international publication and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may prevent international publication by withdrawing the international application; international publication may be postponed by withdrawing the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to paragraph 9.023A for preventing publication and paragraphs 11.056-11.057 for withdrawing priority claims to postpone publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of designations
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the designation of any State (or certain kinds of protection) by a notice addressed to the IB, RO or IPEA and received before the expiration of 30 months from the priority date; any such withdrawal is free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of withdrawal must be signed by all applicants; agent/common representative may sign if appointed; 'deemed common representative' may not sign for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of withdrawal of designation when State elected for IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of the designation of a State which has been elected for the purposes of international preliminary examination automatically results in withdrawal of the corresponding election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 90bis.2(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation when State designated for both national and regional patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a State has been designated for obtaining both a national patent and a regional patent, withdrawal of the designation of that State is taken to mean withdrawal only of the designation for the purpose of obtaining a national patent, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should make clear which designation is intended to be withdrawn in practice (paragraphs 4.022-4.026 and 5.052-5.053).

rubrics_metrics.name: All designations withdrawn equals application withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: If all designations are withdrawn, the international application itself will be treated as withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 90bis.2(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation not published if withdrawal before technical preparations completed
rubrics_metrics.description: A designation will not be published if the notice of its withdrawal reaches the International Bureau before the technical preparations for international publication have been completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to paragraph 9.014.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheets when designation withdrawal affects applicant identity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application indicates different applicants for different designated States and withdrawal of a designation results in that applicant no longer being an applicant for any designated State, replacement sheets indicating only the remaining applicants should be furnished with the notice of withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant fails to submit replacement sheets, the request is corrected by the receiving Office or the International Bureau, which notifies the other and the applicant accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw a priority claim made in the international application by a notice addressed to the IB, RO, or IPEA and received before the expiration of 30 months from the priority date; any or all priority claims may be withdrawn; such withdrawal is free of charge and must be signed by all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent or appointed representative may sign where appointment effected by signature of certain documents; see Rule 90bis.3 and 90bis.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time limits after withdrawal of a priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Where withdrawal of the priority claim causes a change in the priority date, any time limit computed from the original priority date which has not yet expired is computed from the new priority date resulting from the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not possible to extend a time limit that has already expired when the priority claim is withdrawn. If notice of withdrawal reaches IB after technical preparations for publication, IB may proceed based on the original priority date for publication time limit computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw a supplementary search request at any time prior to transmittal of the supplementary international search report or the declaration that no such report will be established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal will only result in a refund if IB has not yet transmitted any document to the Authority for supplementary search. Notice may be addressed either to IB or to the Authority and is effective on receipt. If notice fails to reach Authority in time to prevent transmittal, the report/declaration will still be communicated to designated Offices. If multiple supplementary requests exist, notice must specify which is withdrawn (Rule 90bis.3bis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for withdrawal of supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of withdrawal of the supplementary search request must be signed by the applicant or, if there are multiple applicants, by all of them, or by the agent/common representative whose appointment has been effected by each applicant signing specified documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature/appointment details tie back to the specific authorizations (see paragraph 11.059).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of demand for international preliminary examination or election
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the demand or the election of any State at any time prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date by a notice addressed to the International Bureau; any such withdrawal is free of charge and must be signed by all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appointed agent or common representative may sign on behalf of those who appointed them, but a 'deemed common representative' may not sign on behalf of other applicants (Article 37, Rule 90bis.4, Rule 90bis.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of withdrawing demand/elections after national time limits in some States
rubrics_metrics.description: In respect of designated Offices which do not apply the 30-month time limit, withdrawing the demand or elections after the expiration of the time limit under Article 22 for entry into the national phase may be treated as a withdrawal of the international application in that State unless the national phase has already started there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawal is effected before expiration of that time limit, the international application will not be considered withdrawn but applicant must take usual steps to enter national phase (Article 37(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time limits generally (Rule 80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 80 contains detailed provisions concerning computation of time limits (years, months or days), including cases where a time limit expires on a non-working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-working days for the IB are published in Official Notices; the PCT Time Limit Calculator (https://pct.wipo.int/ePCTExternal/pages/PctTimeline.xhtml?lang=en) assists applicants. If period starts on date of a notification, may be extended if notification was actually mailed on a later date or received more than seven days after date it bears (see Rule 80.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in mail service (excuse of delay for mail issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 82 provisions govern late arrival or loss due to mail service irregularities (e.g., mail interrupted by strike): they may excuse failure to meet a time limit for up to six months after expiration, provided the document was mailed at least five days before the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing must be by registered airmail or registered surface mail (where surface would normally arrive within two days). Evidence is required and a substitute document must be filed promptly (see Rule 82.1(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of delivery services for excusing delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Some national Offices and intergovernmental organizations apply Rule 82 provisions where a delivery service other than postal authorities is used; offices and circumstances vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 82.1(d)-(e) and Annexes B for which Offices recognize delivery services and in what circumstances Rule 82.1 applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse of delay due to force majeure (Rule 82quater.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 82quater.1 allows excusing delay in meeting time limits where caused by force majeure (war, revolution, civil disorder, strike, natural calamity, epidemic, general unavailability of electronic communications, or similar) in the locality where applicant resides, has a place of business or is staying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The excuse applies only to time limits fixed in the Regulations and not to the priority period or time limit for entering the national phase. Applicant must act as soon as reasonably possible (generally shortly after cause ceases). Request and evidence must be submitted as soon as reasonably possible and, in any case, not later than six months after expiration of the applicable time limit. Examples of acceptable evidence include reliable news reports, official statements, ISP/electricity provider statements. An Office/Authority/IB may waive evidence where it is aware of the event and publishes conditions for waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse for unavailability of electronic means at Office (Rule 82quater.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 82quater.2 allows any Office or intergovernmental organization to provide for a general excuse of delay if failure was due to unavailability of permitted electronic means of communication at that Office or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, the Office/organization notifies the IB which publishes details (including duration) in the Gazette and on WIPO's website. The excuse applies only to time limits fixed in the Regulations and not to priority period or national phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions after failure due to Office electronic unavailability
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant failed to meet a time limit due to unavailability of permitted electronic means at the Office/organization, the applicant must perform the relevant action on the next working day when communications become available and request excuse of delay indicating the cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 11.065C for timing and required statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits by Offices during force majeure (Rule 82quater.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office/Authority/IB may, in exceptional circumstances and due to a force majeure event, establish a period of extension such that time limits fixed in the Regulations are generally extended during the international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be applied where general disruption affects operations (e.g., epidemic, natural disaster, infrastructure damage). Additional periods may be established while disruption continues, but no period may be longer than two months from its start date. The Office/Authority/IB publishes beginning/end dates; any time limit that would expire during that period will, subject to Rule 80.5, expire on the first day after the extension. Applicant need not request the extension. Extensions do not apply to priority period or national phase entry and may not be taken into account by designated/elected Offices if national processing has already started at the time of publication of the extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of letters and documents — general formalities (Rule 92 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters must be signed; any other document submitted must be accompanied by a letter. Letters/documents to RO, ISA, Authority for supplementary search, and IPEA must generally be in the language of the international application or in the language of a transmitted translation; communications to the IB must be in English or French and may be in the language of publication if submitted via ePCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 12.1, Rule 55.2, Rule 92 and Section 104 for detailed requirements. Language of amendments to claims under Article 19 and demands/amendments under Article 34 have specific references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means and format of filing documents (electronic/paper/facsimile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each national Office or Authority specifies means by which documents relating to international applications may be filed; some only accept electronic submissions and may treat paper as not received. An Office may require documents filed on paper be resubmitted electronically within two months; failure will lead to disregard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on e-submission and Office profiles is available via ePCT Office Profile. Rule 92.4 governs facsimile and similar communications: such means may only be used where the Office accepts them. Some Offices require confirmation within 14 days or may treat the communication as not made; failures may be waived in some cases. Originals may be required even if no standing requirement exists. Annexes B provide Office-specific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originals and telecommunication submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents to be submitted are parts of the international application or replacement sheets with amendments/corrections, the original should in any event be mailed as a matter of course on the same or following day when transmitted by telecommunication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check Annexes B before sending documents by telecommunication to ascertain applicable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original accompanying letter identifying earlier transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original is sent to an Office of a document previously transmitted by telecommunication, the original must be accompanied by a letter identifying the date and means of the earlier transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 92.4(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of illegible or incomplete telecommunication transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If part or all of a document received by telecommunication is illegible, or part is not received, the document is treated as not having been received to the extent it is illegible or the attempted transmission failed, and the Office promptly notifies the applicant accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 92.4 — notification obligation of the Office/organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a file reference in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant or appointed agent may mark a file reference on specified forms and correspondence (first sheet of the request form, pages of other elements, first sheet of supplementary search request, first sheet of demand form, and other correspondence). The file reference may consist of Latin letters and/or Arabic numerals and the hyphen character and may not exceed 25 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving Office, IB, ISA, Authority for supplementary search and IPEA will use the file reference in correspondence with the applicant (Section 109).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of international applications before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application is confidential in relation to third parties until the international publication date, with only limited and specified exceptions (Article 30, Article 38, Rule 94.1(a), Rule 94.1bis(a), Rule 94.1ter(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At applicant's request any of IB, RO or ISA will furnish copies of any document in its file subject to reimbursement; a competent court order substitutes for applicant authorization. (Access to IPEA file discussed separately in paragraph 11.074.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of documents after international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After international publication, the international application, published amendments under Article 19, the international search report and copies of priority documents (subject to exceptions) are publicly available and the International Bureau will furnish copies of any document in its file at request upon reimbursement, except for documents omitted from publication or from public file access and documents prepared solely for internal use by the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office and ISA may also furnish copies after publication except for omitted-from-publication documents (see paragraph 9.016A and 11.073A). Refer to Rule 17.2, Rule 48.2 and Rule 94 series for details.
